overview.description: Zwanzigerrufen ('Call the Twenty') is an Austrian Tarot game. 4 players. 40-card deck (from 54-card Industrie und Glück). 20 Tarocks + 20 suit cards. Declarer calls Tarock XX to find secret partner. Win 45+ of 88 card points. Simpler than Königrufen. Trull cards: Pagát(I), Mond(XXI), Sküs = 5pts each.

history.origins: Zwanzigerrufen (or Zwanz'gerrufen) is the leading trick-taking Tarock game in many regions of eastern Austria. It belongs to the European Tarot card game family and uses a 40-card pack derived from the 54-card Industrie und Glück deck. The game is simpler than Königrufen, which is more widely played across Austria, and has been a major regional variant since the 20th century. It influenced Hungarian Tarokk and related Central European Tarock games.
timeline: 20th century: Leading Tarock game in eastern Austria; simpler than Königrufen.
history.evolution: Simpler predecessor of Königrufen. Source for Hungarian Tarokk.

setup.deck: 40 cards: 20 Tarocks (I-XXI minus II,III + Sküs) + 20 suit.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's left cuts. Each player receives 10 cards in two packets of five, forehand first. No talon. Optionally, cutter may knock and dealer places four stacks of 10 for players to choose from, forehand first.

rules.objective: The declarer's team (or soloist) must win at least 45 of the 88 card points in tricks to win the game. In a normal game the calling team plays against the defenders; the first team to reach 45 or more points wins.
rules.gameplay: Declarer calls Tarock XX = secret partner. Follow suit, must trump if void. Trull (I, XXI, Sküs) = 5pts each. K=5, Q=4, Knight=3, J=2, others=1. Total=88.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Deal 10 cards each in two packets of five, forehand first. No talon.

phases.label: Auction
phases.notes: Forehand starts. Call Tarock XX (or XIX down to XVI if holding XX) for secret partner; others may bid or say Weiter until all pass.

phases.label: Play tricks
phases.notes: Forehand leads. Follow suit; must trump if void. No must-head. Tarocks permanent trumps. 10 tricks; 45+ of 88 points to win.

declare.description: Call a tarock (XX, or XIX down to XVI if holding XX) to designate secret partner. Holder of the called card becomes declarer's partner without revealing.
declare.constraints: Forehand must at least call a tarock held by another player. If forehand holds XX through XVI she must play solo.

pass.description: Say Weiter (pass); decline to bid or bid further in the auction.

bid.description: Bid a contract: Normal game (call XX for partner), Suit Solo (Faberln), or Solo (Schwarzer). Normal = 1 point; Solos = 4–5 points. Solo overrides Suit Solo.
bid.constraints: Forehand begins auction. Each player in turn may bid or pass (Weiter). Bidding continues until all have passed.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Sküs, XXI down to I (higher number beats lower); Pagat beats Sküs and Mond when all three in same trick (Märchenstich).
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must follow suit; if void must play tarock; no obligation to head the trick.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Forehand leads first trick; then trick winner leads.

edgeCases.text: When Sküs, Mond and Pagat meet in same trick, Pagat wins (Märchenstich).
Optional rule to throw in hand before play if no tarocks or only Trulls; same dealer redeals; game does not count.
In Suit Solo tarocks are not trumps; caller must have 5+ suit cards; only Valat, Absolute, 4 Kings bonuses apply.

engine.handRankingSystem: Trick points: Trull (I, XXI, Sküs) 5 each; K=5, Q=4, Knight=3, J=2, others=1; total 88. Higher tarock beats lower; Pagat beats Sküs and Mond when all in same trick (Märchenstich).
engine.deckDescription: A 40-card Industrie und Glück tarock pack used for Zwanzigerrufen: 20 tarocks and 20 suit cards. The tarocks are Skus, I, and IV through XXI.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits remain in reduced form: black suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, 10 while red suits keep King, Queen, Cavalier, Jack, Ace.
engine.rankDescription: Trumps are Skus, I, and IV through XXI. In the suits, black cards keep 10 as the only pip and red cards keep Ace as the only pip beneath the courts.
